elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each party.
elements.evidence: No monetary liability cap is imposed. Instead, the clause waives certain liability and makes specified Servicer and Marketing Agent obligations uncapped.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes fees paid or payable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no fees-based cap or reference to fees paid or payable.

elements.element: The fee-based limb measures fees over the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: No 12-month lookback period or claim-based measurement date appears.

elements.element: The cap includes a USD 1,000,000 limb.
elements.evidence: No USD 1,000,000 amount appears.

elements.element: The cap equals the greater of the fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The required greater-of formulation is absent.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion of indirect damages for any party.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion of consequential damages for any party.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality obligations are not mentioned or expressly preserved from the waiver or any limitation.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Data protection obligations are not mentioned or expressly preserved.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Security obligations are not mentioned or expressly preserved.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly includes indemnification obligations under Section 6.3 among obligations that “will not be subject to any limitation or cap on liability.”

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The Depositor, Servicer and Marketing Agent are each expressly liable for gross negligence in performing their obligations, and the clause imposes no monetary cap on that liability.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The Depositor, Servicer and Marketing Agent are each expressly liable for “willful misconduct,” with no monetary cap imposed.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is not identified; the reference to bad faith is not an express fraud carve-out.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No intellectual-property infringement carve-out appears, and there is no direction protecting infringement claims concerning the other party's IP.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for purposes of the cap.
elements.evidence: The clause does not characterize payment obligations as non-damages. References to deposits, remittances and acquisition obligations being uncapped do not supply the required characterization.

elements.element: A liability cap applies mutually to each party.
elements.evidence: No monetary cap applies to the parties; the clause instead uses waivers and uncapped treatment for selected obligations.

elements.element: The mutual cap equals 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: There is no cap based on 12 months' fees.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: The rendered language expressly states that indemnification obligations under Section 6.3 are not subject to any limitation or cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality carve-out or express preservation of confidentiality liability appears.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Gross-negligence liability is expressly preserved for the Depositor, Servicer and Marketing Agent, and no monetary cap limits it.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Willful-misconduct liability is expressly preserved for the Depositor, Servicer and Marketing Agent, and no monetary cap limits it.

result.reason: The redline does not implement either required liability-cap structure. It adds broad uncapped treatment for the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's specific and core performance obligations, rather than a mutual fees-based cap with defined carve-outs, and omits the damages exclusion, confidentiality carve-out and other required protections. The added provision is also broader than necessary and asymmetrical because it does not similarly amend the Depositor provision. Although readable, “none of which” has an uncertain referent and the interaction between the broad waiver, preserved specific obligations and misconduct provisions is not cleanly structured.
